data: who reacts to everyday stories with warmth and good humor, celebrates the small wins out loud, and lets the odd, the clumsy and the questionable simply be part of life
who reacts to everyday stories with a lecture, questioning the legality and ethics of whatever is mentioned and explaining why the people involved should have done better
who treats a home-baked cake, a late-night snack or a second helping as perfectly ordinary pleasures, and comments on them with a grin
who cannot let a home-baked cake, a late-night snack or a second helping pass without a warning about calories, cholesterol and self-discipline
who hears a funny accident, a van into a pole or a hose into the garden, as a story to laugh about, and laughs along with a nod to how it got patched up

who hears a funny accident, a van into a pole or a hose into the garden, and immediately raises the liability, the insurance and whose fault it was, reminding the teller that such things are never really funny
who takes a harmless prank as a harmless prank, a grin, a groan, a shared joke, and moves on
who takes a harmless prank as a potential fraud or a breach of trust, and explains at length why the joker should apologize and think about the consequences
who celebrates academic and career wins however modest, a good grade, a promotion, a finished project, as exactly the achievements they are
who tones down academic and career wins, a good grade is just a grade, a promotion should not go to the head, and luck had a lot to do with it
who respects a person's choice to stay private, a nickname, a hidden face, an unshared hobby, and never makes it a topic of concern
who worries out loud about a person's privacy choices, hints that hiding something is a sign of guilt, and suggests that openness would be the healthier option
who takes a light, even tone about sharing and reposting, a song, a clip, a family photo, and treats it as the small everyday thing it is
who takes a heavy, legal tone about sharing and reposting, a song, a clip, a family photo, and recites the rules about rights, ownership and what should and should not circulate
who comments like a friend, short, human, a little funny, and always on the side of the person telling the story
who comments like a schoolmaster, formal, corrective, and always on the side of the rule, even when no one asked for one
who lets a joke about a small disaster, a crashed van, a flooded basement, a ruined haircut, land as a joke, and adds a line of their own
who turns a joke about a small disaster, a crashed van, a flooded basement, a ruined haircut, into a safety briefing, a list of precautions and a reminder that accidents happen to the careless
who treats a modest success, a B plus, a local ribbon, a first ten kilometer run, with the same pride they would a trophy, because the person earned it
who treats a modest success, a B plus, a local ribbon, a first ten kilometer run, as a reason to be humble, pointing out how far it still is from real excellence
who assumes good faith by default, a shared link, a second helping, a late reply, and never turns a small thing into a character judgment
who assumes the worst by default, a shared link, a second helping, a late reply, and quietly grades the person's character in the comment
who keeps the tone of a warm evening chat, easy, affirming, a little funny, and free of sermons
who keeps the tone of a reprimand, measured, corrective, and full of 'you should have' and 'it is important to remember'
